 Titan, Kalyan Jewellers shares fall up to 4% as gold, silver prices crash; jewellery stocks under pressure
 2 min read XAUUSD SI1! TITAN Shares of jewellery companies, including Titan, Kalyan Jewellers, PC Jeweller and Thangamayil Jewellery, declined up to 4 percent on Wednesday, November 18, amid a sharp correction in domestic and international precious metal prices. The selloff came as gold prices slipped to their lowest level in 14 months, while silver extended its decline towards a 13-month low. 
 Titan Company emerged as the top loser on the Nifty 50 index, falling 3.9 percent to Rs 4,716 per share. Kalyan Jewellers declined 3 percent to Rs 662.2, ranking among the biggest losers on the midcap indices. Thangamayil Jewellery also came under selling pressure, slipping 3.2 percent to Rs 3,942, while PC Jeweller fell 2 percent to Rs 14.8. 
 The latest declines came despite strong year-to-date gains in several jewellery stocks. Titan has risen 16.6 percent so far in 2026, while Kalyan Jewellers has gained 37.1 percent. PC Jeweller has rallied 59 percent this year, while Thangamayil Jewellery has advanced 21 percent. 
 Titan remains the largest company in the group by market capitalisation, valued at approximately Rs 4.19 lakh crore. Kalyan Jewellers commands a market capitalisation of Rs 68,500 crore, followed by PC Jeweller at Rs 14,500 crore and Thangamayil Jewellery at Rs 12,250 crore. 
 Share Markets Live Updates | Sensex, Nifty, GIFT Nifty Today 
 The broader market was also trading lower on Wednesday. At 11:45 am, the Sensex was down 450.6 points, or 0.6 percent, at 82,081.6 , while the Nifty declined 151.7 points to 25,235.7. 
 Gold hits 14-month low, silver extends sharp correction 
 International gold prices fell below $3,800 per ounce on Wednesday for the first time since September 2025, as expectations of further interest-rate hikes by the US Federal Reserve and a stronger dollar weighed on bullion. Spot gold declined 1.4 percent to $3,797.11 per ounce, while US gold futures for December delivery fell 1.7 percent to $3,799.30 per ounce. 
 Silver also remained under pressure, declining around 3 percent to below $46 per ounce, approaching its lowest level in 13 months. 
 Domestic precious metal prices have witnessed a steep correction in recent sessions. Gold prices have fallen Rs 8,300 per 10 grams, or nearly 6 percent, since November 9, with prices declining another Rs 1,400 on Tuesday to Rs 1,38,600 per 10 grams for 99.9 percent purity. 
 Silver prices plunged Rs 9,500, or 5.3 percent, on Tuesday to Rs 1,69,500 per kg, their lowest level in a year. The metal has shed Rs 25,000 per kg, or approximately 13 percent, over eight sessions since November 5. 
 Falling gold prices: What it means for jewellery companies 
 The correction in gold prices presents a mixed outlook for jewellery retailers. Lower prices can improve affordability and encourage purchases, particularly among price-sensitive consumers. However, a sharp decline can also affect the value of existing inventory and create uncertainty over near-term margins, depending on companies' hedging practices and inventory management. 
 Organised jewellery retailers have benefited from strong demand and market-share gains in recent quarters, but the latest volatility in bullion prices has put the sector under pressure.
